DW-CAP-COMMUNITY-BACKUP-RESTORE.rationale: Backup and restore are bounded operator workflows; public exposure would weaken operational safety.

operations: represent configured, unavailable, degraded, and stale states

DW-CAP-COMMUNITY-WORKER-SCHEDULER.rationale: The durable worker and scheduler are machine consumers; ordinary users must not invoke queue or lease primitives.

DW-CAP-COMPATIBILITY-OBSERVATION.rationale: The retained observer is deprecated compatibility evidence and must not regain an ordinary active consumer.

DW-CAP-DEVELOPMENT-OPERATIONAL-TOOLING.rationale: Development and validation operations are intentionally consumed by developers and CI rather than exposed as product actions.

DW-CAP-DOCUMENTATION-GOVERNANCE-CATALOG.rationale: Ledgerlight validators and generators are repository automation consumers, not product UI.

DW-CAP-GOVERNED-VERIFICATION-CONTROL-PLA.rationale: Sounding Line is a verification control plane consumed by CI and authorized local runners.

DW-CAP-IMMUTABLE-PUBLISHING-EDITIONS-FOR.rationale: Immutable publishing, checksums, forks, and version history are consumed. The current comparison consumer still presents storage-oriented paths and serialized values instead of the governed Tideglass semantic projection.

DW-CAP-INTEGRATED-WHOLE-PRODUCT-VOYAGE.rationale: All locally implemented Homeport journeys consume their accepted contracts; the remaining owner decision is an acceptance rung, not an unused operation.

DW-CAP-PRIVATE-BACKUP-RESTORE.rationale: Private-content backup and restore remain bounded operator workflows with no public consumer.

operations: represent unavailable, degraded, and stale states

DW-CAP-PRIVATE-REPAIR-OPERATIONS.rationale: Repair execution is security restricted and intentionally available only to approved operators with audit evidence; no generic public or account-owner repair surface is allowed.

DW-CAP-PUBLIC-ORIGIN-TRUST-BOUNDARY.rationale: The trust boundary is consumed by server-side redirect and message construction code and has no safe user-invoked operation.

DW-CAP-SECURITY-PRIVACY-PLATFORM.rationale: Security primitives are consumed through owning services and allowlisted projections; raw rate-limit, credential, scanner, and concurrency internals are intentionally withheld from ordinary users.

DW-CAP-TRANSACTIONAL-EMAIL-DELIVERY.rationale: Delivery is consumed by account flows, but safe health and receipt lifecycle truth has no authenticated operator projection on accepted main.

DW-CAP-VERIFICATION-PROVIDER-FRAMEWORK.rationale: The simulator, request lifecycle, Captain override, and recovery are consumed; no accepted real provider emits the evidence envelope.

newFindings.rootCause: The accepted comparePublishedVersions path compares serialized snapshot fields and the Studio consumer renders internal paths and before/after serialized values. It does not consume a schema-normalized semantic Change Set or audience-safe Tideglass projection.
newFindings.currentBehavior: Creator Studio provides Compare to current, but its result is a storage-oriented structured diff rather than governed semantic edition intelligence.
newFindings.expectedBehavior: All edition-comparison consumers use the deterministic Tideglass semantic comparison authority, preserve exact edition identities and checksums, and receive the audience-safe projection appropriate to the requesting role.
newFindings.assignedProjectPhase: Tideglass and Shipwright owner-coordinated follow-on; no later phase is started by Deepwater
newFindings.mainlineDependency: Accepted Tideglass semantic comparison authority plus owner-coordinated Studio consumer migration
newFindings.closureEvidence: Accepted-main Tideglass semantic engine and safe projection replace the storage-oriented comparison consumer; focused semantic, privacy, and Studio integration tests pass; Sounding Line accepts the owner slice.
